problems.problem: The generated ground contradicts the declared 'continuous honed sandstone ground': a raised tiled curb/step band with visible grout joints and a hard top edge runs across the frame at y≈1150-1245 behind the bottle, reading as a low platform skirting rather than a seamless floor. The bottle's base line (y=1239) lands exactly on the curb's bottom joint, so the flacon appears parked against a step instead of standing on the continuous stone plane the concept promises.

The promised 'soft broad cloud-shadow band' renders as a muddy brown smudge floating at y≈430-660 in the left wall field, directly behind and around the GUCCI logo and the top of the title column. It darkens the exact zone the editorial column occupies, muddying ink contrast and looking like a stain rather than diffuse daylight modulation.

The teal ledger rule is broken: only a ~6px dash is visible at approximately (383,576); the intended vertical margin rule closing the title column fails to render at legible length, so the declared 'ledger column' device is absent and the left column loses its closing edge.

Hierarchy inside the left column is under-resolved: the GUCCI brand line at 30px with 6px tracking sits 94px above the 84px title with a large dead gap, and the column head floats without a baseline relation to the rule; compared with the references' confident editorial blocks (dense caption tiers, clear optical alignment), this column reads sparse and slightly accidental despite correct clearance from the bottle.

Contact detail (crop 466,1099-1003,1349) confirms a real, correctly seated contact shadow: soft occlusion hugs the full base footprint with offset_y=0, no floating. However the shadow is thinner and lighter than the ambient light logic of the scene: the diffuse overcast-warm daylight on the matte stone in references of this type carries a broader, slightly deeper occlusion halo; here the footprint reads a touch sticker-like at the outer corners of the base.
